purpose: Direct comparison of the frozen CDM 3.0.3 (catalogue 3.1.1 findings and metadata) with BugSigDB, a human-curated signature database, on the papers present in both. Scoring rules, thresholds and endpoints are fixed in this file before the run; its sha256 is written to PREREGISTRATION.sha256 in the output folder before any result is computed.
paper_matching: CDM paper.pmid == BugSigDB PMID, else lower-cased CDM paper.doi == BugSigDB DOI. No title matching.

our_findings.primary: claim rows with claim_source = 'catalogue_v3_1' (the frozen catalogue 3.1.1 findings)

bugsigdb_signatures: all signatures of matched papers whose 'Abundance in Group 1' is increased or decreased; taxon = last NCBI ID of each ';'-separated lineage

taxon_matching.exact: same NCBI Taxonomy ID -> verdict MATCH
taxon_matching.lineage: both IDs lifted to their genus in nodes.dmp (IDs at genus rank or above are kept as they are) and the lifted IDs are equal -> verdict PARTIAL
taxon_matching.otherwise: MISMATCH; OURS_MISSING when the paper has no linked taxon in our findings

region_16s.rule: MATCH if the BugSigDB V-region set equals the set parsed from one of our strings or their union; PARTIAL if they overlap

country.rule: country names and official names (pycountry) plus a fixed alias list (USA, UK, PRC, UAE, Korea, England, ...) mapped to ISO alpha-2

statistical_test.rule: fixed regex classes listed in compare.py:TESTS; BugSigDB values outside these classes are UNCLASSIFIED and excluded

group_size.rule: BugSigDB group 0/1 sample size appears as an integer among our counts

embedding.candidate_split: our strings split on ';' ',' '|' ' vs ' ' versus '; pieces of 2-200 characters
embedding.score: maximum cosine similarity between the BugSigDB value and any candidate of the same paper
embedding.threshold_rule: per field and model: the 95th percentile of the same score computed against the candidates of every OTHER matched paper (cross-paper null). Fixed by rule, never tuned on observed matches.
embedding.lexical: a normalised exact or word-bounded containment match is reported alongside as a strict lower bound

primary: taxon coverage: share of BugSigDB (paper, taxon) items with verdict MATCH or PARTIAL (catalogue findings)
taxon direction concordance: among items matched in both with a single direction on each side, share with the same direction
secondary: support rate of our taxa: share of our (paper, taxon) items present in BugSigDB (not precision: BugSigDB is not exhaustive)
per metadata field: completeness (share of items with an our-side value) and concordance (MATCH share among items with values on both sides)
secondary findings source (all claims) for taxon coverage

chance_baseline: every metric is also computed with each paper's BugSigDB items scored against every OTHER matched paper's extraction (all cross-paper pairs, deterministic). Chance-corrected agreement = (observed - chance) / (1 - chance).
adjudication: for rule-based fields with verdict MISMATCH, both values are looked up with the same rules in the paper's own section text (local, read-only; References and Acknowledgements excluded): OURS_ONLY_IN_TEXT, BSDB_ONLY_IN_TEXT, BOTH_IN_TEXT, NEITHER_IN_TEXT. No text leaves the machine.
ontology_currency: BugSigDB taxon IDs are checked against our NCBI Taxonomy snapshot (2026-11-02): ID present or absent, and BugSigDB leaf name equal or different from the current scientific name. Reported as measured counts only.
reporting_rules: Describe results as concordance with human curation (BugSigDB), never as accuracy.
Disagreement is not automatically our error: BugSigDB curates selected signatures, and adjudication shows which side the text supports.
Taxa we report that are absent from BugSigDB are not counted as false positives.
Direction concordance depends on group orientation (BugSigDB group 1 vs our comparison); report it with that caveat.
